Giorgetti is a member of the right-wing League party whose leader, Deputy Premier and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini, has repeatedly expressed scepticism about the policy of supporting Kyiv. Indeed, Salvini said he would seek to stop Italy's economic and military support for Ukraine after being re-elected League leader last month. Nevertheless, Tajani is confident that that the 13th package of aid for Ukraine since the Russian invasion in 2022 will go through without problem. "The package regarding the shipment of arms to Kyiv, which, being a classified document, must be signed in person," Tajani told Rai radio. "It has already been signed by (Defence Minister Guido) Crosetto and myself, and it has received the formal stamp of approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF). "Minister Giorgetti, who supports the measure, was in Brussels yesterday and could not sign it in person. "He will sign it as soon as he arrives in Rome.
